meeting-notes-vs-minutes.23: Before the next meeting, Lynkk also prepares a Meeting Brief with open action items, which makes approving last meeting's minutes quick, and Ask Lynkk lets you search every past decision and links the exact moment.
meeting-notes-vs-minutes.27: Usually a secretary, clerk or designated note-taker. In boards and associations, the secretary is typically responsible, and the chair approves the final minutes. The note-taker should not also chair the meeting, since running a discussion and recording it at the same time usually means both are done badly.
meeting-notes-vs-minutes.13: Stick to the past tense and neutral wording, and skip direct quotes unless someone's precise phrasing matters.
meeting-notes-vs-minutes.19: Brevity wins, provided 3 things are complete: each decision, each vote, and each action with an owner and date.
